title: Motorola Signature 27 launched: 200MP camera, Gemini AI, 7,000mAh battery and GrapheneOS support — what’s new?
snippet: Motorola has launched the Signature 27 flagship smartphone with a 200MP camera, Gemini AI features, a 12,000-nit display and a 7,000mAh battery. It also offers 100x zoom, GrapheneOS support and seven years of OS upgrades. Global availability is expected in the coming months, starting at $1,599.

title: COD Mobile turns 7: What is new as Verdansk returns with Battle Royale upgrades, Mythic Drops and Ford Racing rewards
snippet: Call of Duty: Mobile's Season 10 update marks its seventh anniversary with the return of Verdansk, new Battle Royale features, two Mythic Drops, the Signal 50 sniper rifle and a Ford Racing collaboration offering over 20 rewards.

title: ‘Your voice matters’: Sarvam AI CEO Pratyush Kumar offers lifetime access to 70-year-old speech-impaired cancer survivor
snippet: Sarvam AI CEO Pratyush Kumar has offered lifetime access to the company's AI models to 70-year-old oral cancer survivor Raghunath AS after he highlighted the need for affordable text-to-speech technology to help people with speech disabilities communicate independently.

title: India focused on becoming AI application capital of the world: Ashwini Vaishnaw
snippet: India is focused on becoming the artificial intelligence (AI) "application capital" of the world, Union Electronics and Information Technology Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said.

title: Motorola Signature 27 launched with 7,000mAh battery, 200MP camera and Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6: Price, features
snippet: Motorola Signature 27 has debuted in global markets with a 200MP periscope camera, 7,000mAh battery, Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 chipset and a 12,000-nit AMOLED display. Priced at $1,599 (approximately  ₹1.51 lakh), the flagship is expected to launch in India soon.

title: Meta, Google and TikTok sue California over new law restricting social media features for teens under 16
snippet: Meta, Google and TikTok have sued California Attorney General Rob Bonta, challenging a new law that restricts autoplay videos and personalised feeds for users under 16. The law, scheduled to take effect in January 2027, could impose fines of up to $50,000 per affected minor for non-compliance.
